name: United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2026-2030)

framework.name: Human Capital and Well-being
framework.description:
Armenia is well-positioned to transform its human capital into a driver of inclusive growth and resilience. While there are development constraints, such as regional disparities, demographic shifts, and gaps in access to quality services, these also offer entry points for systemic reform. Strategic investment in education, health, and social protection, particularly for underserved groups and groups at risk of being left behind, can reduce inequality, significantly improve well-being and the fulfilment of socio-economic rights, thus strengthening social mobility and cohesion. Unlocking this potential requires stronger institutional capacity, targeted financing, and inclusive responsive public policies that consider demographic trends to ensure equitable and resilient human capital development. 

This outcome will be achieved through four interdependent pathways focused on education, health, social protection, and demographic resilience. Each contributes to individual well-being and the fulfilment of socio-economic rights, including the right to education, health, an adequate standard of living, and the rights of children, persons with disabilities, persons living in or near poverty, including in rural areas, and other groups at risk of being left behind, while reinforcing broader societal and economic stability.

children.name: Human Capital & Well-being
children.description: By 2030, people, particularly the most vulnerable, enjoy higher quality, inclusive and gender responsive, and shock responsive services and develop their full potential to lead healthy and resilient lives.

children.name: Education
children.description: The UN will support the implementation of Armenia’s youth policy through the creation of enabling regulatory frameworks, youth engagement platforms, and professionalized youth worker networks, ensuring that young people, including adolescent girls, boys, and those in vulnerable communities, are actively involved in shaping education and skills agendas. Digital learning infrastructure and inclusive, gender-sensitive curricula will be scaled up to foster critical thinking, civic engagement, and lifelong learning, preparing all learners not only for employment but also for active citizenship and community resilience.

children.name: Health
children.description: The UN will contribute by supporting the development and implementation of rights-based health policies and strategies that advance universal health coverage, strengthen primary health care, and integrate nutrition and mental health as core components of service delivery. Emphasis will be placed on preparedness and response capacities, including building a shock-responsive and sustainably financed health system that can withstand public health emergencies and climate-related challenges.

children.name: Social Protection
children.description: The UN will contribute by supporting the development and implementation of comprehensive national social protection policies that expand coverage, improve benefit adequacy, and integrate care and child protection priorities. Policy and technical support will facilitate the professionalization and regulation of the child protection workforce at local levels, introducing measures to prevent and respond to violence, neglect, and unnecessary separation of children from families.

children.name: Demographic Resilience
children.description: The UN will support the enhancement of Armenia’s demographic data systems, including census, population registry, and vital statistics, to provide high-quality, disaggregated evidence for policymaking. This will help ensure that fertility, ageing, and migration trends are effectively integrated into national development strategies. Access to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services, including family planning, will be expanded to enable individuals and couples to achieve their fertility goals. Policies and community programmes promoting healthy and active ageing will be advanced, alongside measures to monitor and address migration patterns, particularly in rural and border areas. Youth participation in demographic policy dialogue will be encouraged to ensure intergenerational perspectives are reflected in resilience strategies.

framework.name: Inclusive Economic Development
framework.description:
Armenia’s economy has shown signs of resilience and dynamism in recent years, maintaining positive trends in GDP growth and advances in key sectors. Nonetheless, the country faces hurdles, such as income inequalities, limited access to decent jobs, low labor productivity, especially in rural areas, weak connectivity to markets and insufficient digital and physical infrastructure. These barriers disproportionately impact women, youth, rural communities, persons with disabilities, refugees and migrants, and other groups at risk of being left behind. Economic growth is heavily reliant on remittances and narrow export bases, with the manufacturing sector remaining underdeveloped. Regulatory issues and weak private sector engagement also hinder innovation and sustainable growth. Strategic investments in livelihoods, local economies, and skills development, paired with inclusive policies, including support for the care economy, can transform Armenia’s economic trajectory. Unlocking this potential requires private sector engagement, effective institutions, and infrastructure that leaves no one behind. 

This outcome will be realized through seven interdependent pathways: livelihoods, local economic development, food systems, decent work, gender equality, smart infrastructure, and cultural heritage. These pathways aim to strengthen Armenia’s resilience and equity while advancing green, inclusive, and innovation-driven growth. They will also contribute to the fulfilment of gender equality and social, economic and cultural rights, including the right to food, decent work, and an adequate standard of living.

children.name: Inclusive Economic Development
children.description: By 2030, people benefit from green, inclusive, economic development, sustainable livelihoods and decent work opportunities.

children.name: Livelihoods
children.description: The UN is supporting the launch of an Inclusive Livelihoods National Framework for Refugees and Host Communities. The Framework aims to address not only the immediate vulnerabilities of the refugees but also the systemic challenges impeding their socio-economic integration. By adopting a structured roadmap for promoting self-reliance, enhancing social cohesion, and ensuring long-term stability, the Framework serves as a key instrument for operationalizing Armenia’s transition from humanitarian response to sustainable development—consistent with the principles of the humanitarian–development–peace (HDP) Nexus. It underscores the importance of evidence-based policies, robust financing, and well-coordinated interventions that go beyond short-term humanitarian assistance. The five key pillars for intervention include: 1) Co-financing for cash support; 2) Social housing; 3) Employment programmes; 4) Support for small businesses and self-employment; and 5) Livelihood support for non-engaged groups.

children.name: Local Area-Based Economic Development
children.description: The UN will contribute by supporting localised policy and institutional reforms that foster private sector development, entrepreneurship, and investments in micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). These efforts will help improve productivity, enable the adoption of low-carbon technologies, and expand access to local, national, and regional markets. Capacity-building for business support services and workers’ organizations will enhance employment opportunities and promote labour rights at the community level. Training systems will be aligned with labour market needs and complemented by lifelong learning opportunities, targeting groups facing barriers to employment such as women, youth, persons with disabilities, and those in rural or border areas.

children.name: Food Systems
children.description:
The UN will support this transformation by providing policy advice and technical expertise to design and implement cross-sectoral food and nutrition strategies, facilitating institutional capacity-building, and supporting investments in climate-smart agriculture, digital solutions, and environmentally sustainable value chain development. It will also contribute to the strengthening of   markets, logistics, and infrastructure connecting farmers to urban consumers.

The UN will also help establish participatory governance mechanisms, promote nutrition-sensitive social protection and school feeding programs, and strengthen food security and nutrition data systems. These efforts will improve rural livelihoods, contribute to poverty reduction, foster healthier diets, and support Armenia’s transition to a low-carbon, innovation-driven economy while promoting environmental sustainability and social cohesion.

agencies.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

children.name: Decent Work
children.description: The UN will advance decent work through support to active labour market policies, social dialogue, and the enforcement of international labour standards. This includes strengthening labour inspection systems, promoting occupational safety and health, and supporting the transition from informal to formal employment. Partnerships with the private sector will focus on green job creation in renewable energy, sustainable tourism, agri-business, and care economy sectors, with targeted interventions for youth, women, and persons with disabilities. Skills development programmes will integrate digital, green, and entrepreneurial competencies, aligning with Armenia’s economic diversification strategies.

children.name: Women's Economic Empowerment and Inclusive Growth
children.description: The UN will support this transformation by providing technical and policy assistance to eliminate labor market discrimination, reform labor and social protection policies, and strengthen care infrastructure. It will promote digital inclusion initiatives to improve women’s access to technology and entrepreneurship opportunities, build institutional capacity for gender-responsive economic planning, and leverage Armenia’s cultural heritage to promote sustainable tourism and creative industries. These efforts will increase women’s labor force participation, drive inclusive and smart economic growth, and diversify livelihoods, particularly for women, youth, and rural communities.

agencies.name: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe

children.name: Sustainable Urban and Infrastructure Development
children.description:
The UN will work with Armenia to gradually strengthen inclusive and climate-resilient infrastructure, in line with relevant global commitments such as the New Urban Agenda. Efforts will focus on improving basic connectivity, public services, and access to markets, including in rural and border areas, while encouraging the use of greener technologies where feasible. Collaboration with national and local authorities, the private sector, and other partners will help integrate sustainability considerations into urban planning, transport, and trade-related infrastructure in a way that supports balanced local development and economic opportunities.

The UN will also provide technical support for the preparation of a National Spatial Strategy and a National Urbanisation Strategy to guide balanced territorial development, strengthen urban-rural integration, and align sectoral policies with sustainable economic growth and cohesion objectives. The UN will work to improve urban economies and livelihoods by supporting secondary cities and towns in Armenia to develop urban and territorial economic strategies that diversify local economies, identify growth poles, optimize value chains that create jobs. It will promote sustainable livelihoods through circular economy initiatives, sustainable construction practices, and renewable energy solutions in urban areas.

children.name: Cultural and Natural Heritage
children.description: The UN will support this transformation by strengthening policies and institutional frameworks for cultural heritage protection, promoting sustainable tourism standards, and building capacity among local communities and creative entrepreneurs. Efforts will include promoting eco-tourism value chains, integrating local food and crafts into tourism offerings, and ensuring benefits are widely shared. In addition, the UN will promote the harnessing of cultural heritage and tourism in urban and peri-urban areas to create inclusive economic opportunities, especially for women and youth. These efforts will ensure that cultural assets are preserved for future generations while unlocking their potential to support resilient, environmentally responsible, and socially inclusive economic development.

framework.name: Green Transition for Resilience
framework.description:
Armenia is increasingly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation. Floods, droughts, and other risks and disasters are intensifying, affecting livelihoods, food security, and public health—especially in rural and marginalized communities and among vulnerable groups, such as children, persons with disabilities and older persons. Unsustainable land and water use, air and soil pollution, and weak regulatory enforcement threaten natural ecosystems and economic stability. Despite these risks, Armenia has a window of opportunity to shift toward a more sustainable and resilient development path—by investing in climate adaptation, low-emission solutions, and inclusive natural resource management. The upcoming COP17, which Armenia will host in 2026, offers a strategic platform to accelerate national commitments and strengthen international partnerships on climate and biodiversity action. Advancing the green transition will require robust policies, cross-sectoral coordination, and broad public engagement. 

This outcome will be achieved through four mutually reinforcing pathways: climate action and natural resource management, disaster risk reduction, biodiversity protection, and public awareness and shared responsibility.

children.name: Green Transition for Resilience
children.description: By 2030, climate change adaptation and mitigation, biodiversity protection, and sustainable natural resources management is strengthened, through gender-responsive, inclusive and innovative approaches.

children.name: Climate Action and Natural Resource Management
children.description:
The UN will help Armenia access climate and green finance by developing bankable project pipelines for adaptation and mitigation, fostering public–private partnerships, and mobilizing resources from international funds such as the Green Climate Fund and the Global Environment Facility. Efforts will promote nature-based solutions—including reforestation, agroforestry, watershed restoration, and sustainable land management in erosion-prone and degraded areas—while rehabilitating conflict-affected agricultural lands to boost productivity and reduce competition over resources. Water resource resilience will be strengthened through climate-smart irrigation, drought-resistant crops, and integrated river basin management, including transboundary cooperation where relevant.
Low-emission urban transformation will be supported through renewable energy investments, energy efficiency upgrades in public buildings, and the development of sustainable urban transport systems. In combatting air pollution, the UN will support the government to reduce emissions from buildings, transport, industry, construction, and waste burning, especially in urban areas, and support the development of new partnerships for better financing of investments.

children.name: Disaster Risk Reduction
children.description: The UN will support this transformation by strengthening community-level disaster risk reduction strategies, enhancing local capacities for risk assessment and response, and promoting inclusive participation of youth, civil society, and the private sector. It will also facilitate the use of digital and geospatial tools for risk mapping and early warning and support institutional coordination to integrate disaster risk reduction into climate adaptation and development frameworks. These efforts will reduce vulnerability, save lives, and build social cohesion while safeguarding livelihoods and infrastructure against climate-related and other hazards.

agencies.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

children.name: Biodiversity Protection
children.description:
The UN will support this transformation by providing technical and policy assistance to strengthen institutional capacity for sustainable natural resource management, promote community-based restoration initiatives, and implement the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan. These efforts will improve ecosystem health, enhance climate resilience, and secure the natural capital for the country and a broader region. 

Hosting COP17 in 2026 offers Armenia a unique opportunity to accelerate its biodiversity agenda, showcase national progress, and foster new partnerships for financing and technical cooperation. The UN will leverage this momentum to mobilise investment, align sectoral policies with ecosystem protection goals, and promote regional cooperation on shared ecosystems and migratory species.

children.name: Public Awareness and Shared Responsibility
children.description: The UN will support this by enhancing the communication capacities of the institutions, promoting climate education, public awareness campaigns, and community-based initiatives that build ownership and accountability for environmental stewardship, ensuring that climate responsibility is shared across society.

framework.name: Governance for a Sustainable Future
framework.description:
Armenia has made progress in strengthening its governance institutions, building greater transparency, accountability, and civic participation. Reforms in public administration, anti-corruption, and justice systems provide a strong foundation to deepen democratic governance and uphold human rights. At the same time, opportunities remain to further promote inclusivity, expand civic space, and ensure that all groups—especially women, youth, refugees, and other groups at risk of being left behind — have a voice in shaping public life. By investing in responsive institutions, inclusive decision-making, and digital transformation, Armenia can foster trust between people and the state, reduce inequality, and strengthen resilience to social, economic, and environmental challenges. 

This outcome will be achieved through six interconnected pathways: public administration, inclusive governance, human rights and justice sector reform, migration and asylum management, participatory governance, and social cohesion.

children.name: Governance for a Sustainable Future
children.description: By 2030, governance institutions and systems are more responsive, accountable, and transparent, upholding the rule of law, human rights, gender equality.

children.name: Inclusive Governance
children.description: The UN will work with legislative, electoral, and local government bodies to strengthen legal and institutional frameworks for accountable, inclusive, and transparent governance. This includes supporting electoral reforms in line with international standards, building capacities for fair, transparent, and inclusive elections, and promoting digital tools for electoral management and civic engagement. The UN will encourage inclusive decision-making structures, ensuring representation of women, youth, persons with disabilities, and displaced populations in governance processes. Partnerships with civil society will promote oversight, civic education, and integrity in public office, contributing to long-term stability and peace dividends through stronger trust between citizens and institutions.

children.name: Human Rights and Justice Sector Reform
children.description: The UN will support the implementation of Armenia’s commitments under international human rights law and the recommendations of UN human rights mechanisms by strengthening national institutions, enhancing legal and policy frameworks, and building capacities for rights-based governance. National capacities for crime prevention and criminal justice will be strengthened, including combating transnational organized crime and drug trafficking. Targeted reforms will improve police service delivery, strengthen community–police trust, and enhance accountability in law enforcement. Detention and penitentiary systems will be modernized to meet human rights standards, focusing on rehabilitation and reintegration of offenders.

children.name: Migration and Asylum Management
children.description: With the UN support migration and asylum management will be modernized to ensure they are transparent, efficient, and rights based. The UN will support the digitalization of case management systems, improved inter-agency coordination, and reforms to strengthen policy and legal frameworks, aligning them with international refugee and human rights law. This includes capacity-building for border management and migration authorities, enhancing their ability to process cases efficiently, ensure due process, and protect the rights of migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, and stateless persons. National migration data systems will be strengthened to improve evidence-based policymaking, including through regional cooperation on migration data exchange.

agencies.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees

children.name: Participatory Governance
children.description: The UN will support this transformation by providing technical assistance in the conduct of elections, as well as facilitating inclusive platforms and local decision-making, including through support for youth councils, women’s leadership programmes, and community-driven planning processes, with special outreach to rural and border communities. Institutionalized feedback loops will be established for citizens to provide input on government performance, including digital participation platforms, mobile feedback apps, and in-person community consultations. The UN support will strengthen meaningful participation of civil society in monitoring reforms rough work with parliamentary oversight bodies, human rights institutions, and independent watchdogs. These efforts will empower communities, reinforce inclusive governance, and strengthen Armenia’s social fabric.

children.name: Peace, Social Cohesion and Resilience
children.description:
The UN will also promote inclusive local development and conflict-sensitive planning in border, conflict-affected, and refugee-hosting communities, addressing vulnerabilities and building resilience. Efforts will combine infrastructure rehabilitation, improved service delivery, and participatory local governance platforms that bring together state actors, civil society, refugees, women, and youth to jointly set and monitor development priorities. Community dialogue initiatives, youth and women’s leadership programmes, and targeted behaviour-change campaigns will counter discrimination, disinformation, and harmful social norms that foster mutual understanding and reduce tensions.

These measures will be complemented by community safety and human security initiatives, inclusive policing, legal aid, and disaster risk reduction, including participatory risk assessments and early warning systems in targeted border communities.

projects.name: Natural Resource Governance, Nature-Based Solutions, and Climate Resilience Enhanced
projects.description: FAO will advance sustainable land, water, biodiversity and forest management, ecosystem-based adaptation, and alignment with Armenia’s NDCs. The forestry programme will serve as a flagship for rural green growth, mitigation, and community resilience, with large-scale afforestation, coppice restoration, and energy-efficient technologies reducing pressure on fuelwood. FAO will also support the establishment of a national forest monitoring system, pursue land degradation neutrality, and embed biodiversity conservation through Armenia’s CBD commitments.
projects.outcome: Climate Action and Natural Resource Management

projects.name: Public institutions (electoral management bodies, the parliament, ministries, local government) have improved capacities for effective, responsive, transparent and inclusive governance, steering, legislative processes, decentralisation of powers and services.
Local Economic Development Enhanced
projects.description: FAO will promote diversification beyond commodity agriculture, foster entrepreneurship, and strengthen private-sector participation in rural economies. Territorial diagnostics and agrifood systems planning will guide investments, while inclusive value chain development, vocational training, and access to productive resources will empower vulnerable groups. Heritage-based agritourism, LEADER-aligned eco-tourism, and gastro-tourism will reinforce cultural preservation and community-led growth. E-commerce platforms and rural infrastructure will expand “route to market” pathways, strengthening decent work opportunities and competitiveness. By connecting local producers, SMEs, and rural communities to international gastrotourism networks, FAO will expand market opportunities, strengthen Armenia’s food identity, and generate decent work in rural areas.

projects.name: Disaster Risk Management Strengthened
projects.description: FAO will support integrated, gender-responsive DRM across anticipatory action, early warning, preparedness, risk reduction, response, and recovery in agriculture and rural territories. Support will include multi-hazard risk assessment and geospatial risk mapping, damage and loss accounting to inform compensation and recovery, and mainstreaming early warning into agricultural practices and extension. Through One Health platforms, FAO will strengthen pandemic preparedness, animal health surveillance, biosecurity, and AMR management. Nature-based solutions—such as ecosystem restoration and agroecology—will reduce hazard exposure, while inclusive capacity development will equip local institutions and communities to own and sustain risk governance. The pathway of change is data-driven DRM system that prevents losses, protects rural livelihoods, and accelerates recovery.

projects.name: Digitalization, ICT Infrastructure and Innovation Expanded
projects.description: FAO will promote the digital transformation of Armenia’s agrifood systems by strengthening ICT infrastructure, expanding access to agri-tech solutions, and building institutional and community-level capacities. Digital registries, smart farming tools, innovation incubators and advisory service models will enhance decision-making, agricultural production, post-harvest management, and market access. Local Action Groups and Agricultural Cooperatives will serve as hubs for digital literacy, youth employment, and inclusive service provision. Digital platforms will enable e-advisory services, e-commerce and producer visibility, while agrifood dashboards and data governance systems will support transparency, interoperability, and early warning systems. Finally, FAO will support the development of automated information systems for veterinary, phytosanitary, and food safety sectors to enhance electronic control over regulated product circulation. These systems enable efficient data collection, traceability, and risk-based monitoring, strengthening regulatory oversight and ensuring compliance with international standards. By embedding these digital tools into national systems, FAO will help modernize agrifood governance and improve transparency, accountability, and responsiveness across the value chain.

UNHCR will further pursue adoption and implementation of the draft legislative package amendments for the revision of refugee protection legislation, adoption of the draft Law on Stateless persons, as well as, building on ENS statelessness index findings for Armenia, will aim to advance legislative and policy reforms to further strengthen statelessness protection and prevention standards in the country. projects.name: Refugee and host communities are better prepared for hazards through awareness-raising, localized risk preparedness planning and capacity building
projects.description:
This sub-output focuses on strengthening and operationalizing community-level disaster risk reduction (DRR) strategies and frameworks in high-risk municipalities, ensuring alignment with national disaster risk management systems and mass influx preparedness arrangements.
Building on progress up to May 2026, including DRM plan revisions, digital risk mapping, and contingency planning support, the next phase (May 2026 onward) will consolidate and scale these efforts toward operational, activation-ready DRR systems.
Key activities include:
•	Revision, development, and formal adoption of municipal DRR frameworks incorporating multi-hazard risks and displacement scenarios; 
•	Alignment of community-level DRR frameworks with national contingency planning, early warning systems, and trigger-based activation mechanisms. 
•	Expansion and institutionalization of digital DRM tools and risk mapping platforms. 
•	Validation and testing through drills and simulation exercises. 
•	Capacity strengthening and formal endorsement processes to ensure sustainability and institutional ownership. 
Overall, the focus will be on transitioning from planning-based approaches to operational, trigger-based preparedness systems at community level.

As foundation for peace, social cohesion in refugee-hosting communities is strengthened through inclusive community support initiatives that foster dialogue, joint activities and collaboration between refugees and host community members to realise an environment where all can thrive
projects.description:
This sub-output focuses on strengthening social cohesion in refugee-hosting communities as a foundation for peace, through inclusive and community-driven initiatives that foster dialogue, trust, and mutual understanding between refugees and host community members. Building on a human-centred and foresight-driven approach, UNHCR will support communities not only to engage in dialogue on current challenges, but also to collectively explore and shape their shared futures.
Through participatory platforms, joint activities, and community-based projects, communities will be supported to co-create spaces for interaction, shared ownership, and collective problem-solving at the local level. In addition, foresight methodologies will be introduced to facilitate structured dialogues where refugees and host communities jointly explore possible future scenarios, articulate their preferred vision of peaceful and inclusive communities, and identify practical pathways to achieve them.
Particular attention will be given to the inclusive engagement of women, youth, and other groups at risk of exclusion, ensuring that diverse perspectives inform both present actions and future vision. By strengthening agency and participation, these approaches will enable communities to move from being recipients of support to active co-creators of peaceful and resilient environments.

The competitiveness of export-oriented industries in Armenia in strengthened through ensuring sustainability of the SPACE59 Light Industry Training and Service Center
projects.description:
Since September 2014, UNIDO has supported Armenia in revitalising its garment industry through the Industrial Upgrading and Modernisation Programme. The intervention has focused on strengthening the local garment sector by enhancing the human and technical capacities of beneficiary manufacturers, upgrading the skills of local experts and reinforcing the capacities of national technical support institutions. Over a six-year implementation period, corporate data collected in 2022 demonstrated substantial growth compared to the 2016 baseline, with turnover increasing by 290%, exports by 328%, employment in beneficiary enterprises by 153% and domestic sales by 270%. The project also contributed significantly to job creation and the development of sector-specific skills, particularly benefiting women and youth.

In December 2020, UNIDO, in partnership with the Ministry of Economy of Armenia, facilitated the establishment of the Light Industry Training and Service Center, SPACE59. The centre aims to enhance the competitiveness of the garment and footwear sectors by supporting small and medium-sized enterprises in attracting skilled professionals, adopting innovative upgrading methodologies and accessing high-quality technical services. In addition, SPACE59 supports product development under an umbrella brand to strengthen the sector’s positioning in international markets.

projects.name: The quality infrastructure in Armenia is strengthened
projects.description:
Armenia, as a participant in the European Union Neighbourhood Policy since 2004, entered into the Comprehensive and Enhanced Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with the European Union on 1 March 2021. A key component of CEPA with direct relevance to trade and inclusive and sustainable industrial development in Armenia is Chapter 3 on technical barriers to trade. Effective implementation of this chapter has the potential to significantly enhance Armenia’s trade competitiveness. However, a number of structural weaknesses currently limit the country’s ability to fully benefit from these provisions.

A country’s capacity to reduce and, where possible, eliminate technical barriers to trade is closely linked to the strength, effectiveness and international recognition of its quality infrastructure system. One of the critical pillars of this system is metrology, which ensures the accuracy and reliability of measurements used to demonstrate conformity with technical regulations and standards. Metrology, defined as the science of measurement and its application, remains underdeveloped in Armenia. As a result, Armenian industries and conformity assessment bodies often rely on calibration services provided by foreign laboratories, incurring high costs related to transport, travel and service fees.

An assessment of Armenia’s metrology system highlights that, while basic institutional structures exist, significant gaps remain in terms of technical capacity, international recognition and alignment with European Union and international best practices. Addressing these gaps is essential to strengthening Armenia’s quality infrastructure, improving compliance with international market requirements and supporting the country’s integration into European and global value chains.

projects.description: Institutional strengthening projects have been funded by the Executive Committee since its seventh meeting to provide financial support to Article 5 countries in strengthening national capacities for the timely and effective implementation of ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out activities. These projects facilitate coordination between the concerned country, the Executive Committee, the Multilateral Fund Secretariat and the implementing agencies, and have been fundamental in ensuring broad compliance with the Montreal Protocol. In Armenia, the institutional strengthening project aims to support the adoption and implementation of legislation and regulations to control and monitor the import and use of Montreal Protocol controlled substances and related equipment; ensure accurate and timely collection and reporting of data on the consumption of all controlled substances; strengthen coordination among national agencies and stakeholders; supervise the timely implementation of hydrochlorofluorocarbon (HCFC) phase-out and hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) phase-down activities and the resulting reductions in consumption; promote awareness-raising and information exchange on Montreal Protocol-related issues; and support regional cooperation and participation in Montreal Protocol processes.

projects.description: The Kigali implementation plan for hydrofluorocarbons (HFC), stage I, provides a strategic framework to support Armenia in reducing its consumption of hydrofluorocarbons, which are potent greenhouse gases widely used in refrigeration and air-conditioning. Under the plan, Armenia aims to achieve a 10% reduction from its HFC baseline consumption by 1 January 2029, in line with the Kigali Amendment’s global objective of reducing HFC use by 80% by 2045. The plan предусматривает a comprehensive set of measures, including updates to the regulatory framework, strengthening of industry practices, and promotion of the adoption of environmentally friendly alternative technologies. Through these coordinated actions, Armenia will not only fulfil its international obligations under the Kigali Amendment but also contribute meaningfully to global efforts to mitigate climate change.

The capacities of MSMEs are strengthened towards the establishment of the industrial innovation hub in Armenia
projects.description:
Following the first meeting of the National Coordination Body for the Country Programme for Inclusive and Sustainable Industrial Development in Armenia 2022–2026, held on 6 June 2022, the delegations of UNIDO and Armenia agreed to organise working-level follow-up consultations between UNIDO technical experts and national focal points from the relevant line ministries. The objective was to identify concrete project proposals for development and explore potential resource mobilisation opportunities.

In 2023 and 2024, following technical missions to Yerevan, UNIDO conducted further consultations with representatives of the Ministry of Economy of Armenia, presenting a technical assistance intervention aimed at strengthening the national information and communication technology, innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystems in support of the Strategic Plan for the Development of the Digital Economy in Armenia. In this context, the Ministry of Economy requested UNIDO’s assistance to address key challenges related to small and medium-sized enterprise digitalisation and industrial innovation.

The present project document was developed in close alignment with national development priorities and the specific needs of the Government of Armenia, and outlines a concrete, step-by-step intervention to support policymakers, ecosystem support institutions and small and medium-sized enterprises active in information and communication technology and innovation.
